description: A wave terrain oscillator whose curve is drawn by the superformula, so the shape walked around the landscape can be pushed into spikes and lobes

params.text: Picks one of the 27 terrain formulas, or NONE; the four are laid over each other to make the landscape
Moves the curve across the terrain, -10 to 10
Moves the curve up the terrain, -10 to 10
Sets how wide the curve is drawn, 0 to 4
Sets how tall the curve is drawn, 0 to 4
Turns the curve about its centre, 0 to a full turn
Sets the first symmetry number of the superformula, 0 to 16 in whole steps, which is how many lobes the curve has one way
Sets the second symmetry number, 0 to 16 in whole steps, which is how many lobes it has the other way
Sets the first exponent of the superformula, 0.05 to 5, which is the strongest control over the shape
Turns the first exponent negative, which turns the curve inside out
Sets the second exponent of the superformula, -5 to 5
Sets the third exponent of the superformula, -5 to 5
Sets the first divisor of the superformula, 0.05 to 5
Sets the second divisor of the superformula, 0.05 to 5
Attenuates the voltage at the X jack before it is added to the X knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Y jack before it is added to the Y knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Scale X jack before it is added to the RX knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Scale Y jack before it is added to the RY knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Rotation jack before it is added to the ROT knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the N1 jack before it is added to the N1 knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the N2 jack before it is added to the N2 knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the N3 jack before it is added to the N3 knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the A jack before it is added to the A knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the B jack before it is added to the B knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Puts the view back over the middle of the terrain, without moving the curve
Sets how much of the terrain is drawn on the display, 0.1 to 10; this changes the picture and not the sound
While on, a voice sounds only while its channel of the Gate jack is high; while off, the module sounds all the time

inputs.text: Sets the pitch, 1V per octave, one channel per voice
Opens the voice of each channel while the Gate button beside it is on; with that button off the module sounds whatever is patched here
Modulates that movement, one per volt scaled by the knob below it
Modulates that movement, one per volt scaled by the knob below it
Modulates the width, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates the height, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates that turning, one radian per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates that exponent, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates that exponent, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates that exponent, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates that divisor, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates that divisor, one per volt scaled by the knob beside it
While a cable is patched here the curve is walked by this phase over -5V to 5V and the pitch jack is passed over

outputs.text: The height under the curve as it is walked one way round, -5V to 5V
The height under the curve as it is walked the other way round, which gives a second, related signal for the right channel

notes: drag the blue circle on the display to move the curve, which is the X and Y knobs; drag anywhere else to move the view, which changes nothing in the sound
some settings of the symmetry numbers give a curve that runs off to infinity, which is heard as a spike; the maker's advice is to start with the two numbers equal
the speed of the point around a pointed curve varies enough to upset a filter downstream, so keep to rounder curves where that matters
there is no anti-aliasing at all, so a curve drawn large over a rough terrain aliases badly; scale the curve down to cut the high frequencies
